title: An Appeal May Lie Before a Court as Provided in Sub-Section

content.scenario: A consumer, Kumar, files an appeal before the National Commission against a decision of the State Commission. The National Commission dismisses the appeal, and Kumar wants to challenge this decision in a court.
content.outcome: An appeal may lie before a court from the order of the National Commission, but only as provided in sub-section (1) of section 73 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Otherwise, no appeal shall lie before any court from any order of the National Commission.

user_queries: Under what conditions can an appeal be filed in a court against a decision of the National Commission?
What is the purpose of limiting appeals to a court?
Can an appeal be filed in a court against any order of the National Commission?
